title: Chicken Pot Pie with Drop Biscuits
description: Creamy chicken and vegetables under soft golden drop biscuits—classic pot-pie comfort without rolling out pastry.

ingredients.item: cooked chicken, shredded or finely chopped

substitutions: Use cooked turkey instead of chicken.
Use peas and carrots instead of mixed vegetables.
For very tender meat, shred the chicken finely rather than leaving larger chunks.
If you do not have an oven-safe skillet, make the filling on the stove and transfer it to an 8x8-inch baking dish before adding the biscuits.

steps.text: Make a quick creamy chicken-and-vegetable filling.
Mix the drop-biscuit dough and spoon it over the hot filling.
Bake until the biscuits are golden and cooked through.

cookSteps.text: Melt {{fillButter}} butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Stir in {{fillFlour}} flour and cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Slowly whisk in {{broth}} chicken broth and {{fillMilk}} milk. Cook 3–5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens enough to lightly coat a spoon.

Stir in {{chicken}} cooked chicken, {{vegetables}} frozen mixed vegetables, {{onion}} onion powder, thyme if using, and {{pepper}} black pepper. Simmer 3–4 minutes, until the filling is hot. Take the skillet off the heat.
In a medium bowl, stir together {{biscuitFlour}} flour, {{bakingPowder}} baking powder, and {{salt}} salt.
Cut or rub {{biscuitButter}} cold butter into the flour mixture until you have small crumbly pieces. Stir in {{biscuitMilk}} milk just until a soft, shaggy dough forms. Do not overmix.
Drop the biscuit dough by 6–8 spoonfuls over the hot chicken filling. Leave a little space between the mounds so steam can escape.
Bake at 425°F for 18–22 minutes, until the biscuit tops are golden and the centers are cooked through. If the tops brown too quickly, loosely cover with foil for the last few minutes.
Let the pot pie rest for 5 minutes before serving. The filling will thicken a little as it stands.

storage: Refrigerate covered up to 4 days. Reheat individual portions until steaming hot; the biscuits are best reheated uncovered in the oven or toaster oven so the tops do not get soggy.

title: Homemade Macaroni and Cheese
description: Creamy homemade macaroni and cheese with a simple cheddar sauce—rich, cozy, and made from ordinary pantry and fridge staples.
substitutions: Use medium or mild cheddar if you prefer a gentler cheese flavor.
Use half cheddar and half Monterey Jack for an extra-melty sauce.
Use shells or another small pasta shape instead of elbows.
If the sauce gets thicker than you like, stir in a splash of milk before serving.

steps.text: Cook the macaroni until just tender.
Make a smooth cheese sauce with butter, flour, milk, and cheddar.
Stir the macaroni into the cheese sauce and serve hot.

cookSteps.text: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil. Add {{macaroni}} elbow macaroni and cook according to the package directions until just tender. Drain well.
While the pasta cooks, melt {{butter}} butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in {{flour}} flour and cook for 1 minute, whisking constantly.
Slowly whisk in {{milk}} milk. Keep whisking and cook 4–6 minutes, until the sauce is smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon.
Turn the heat to low. Add {{salt}} salt, {{pepper}} black pepper, and mustard powder if using. Stir in {{cheddar}} shredded cheddar a handful at a time until completely melted and smooth.
Add the drained macaroni to the cheese sauce and stir until every piece is coated. If it seems too thick, stir in a small splash of milk.
Taste, adjust the salt and pepper if needed, and serve while hot and creamy.

storage: Refrigerate covered up to 4 days. Reheat gently with a splash of milk, stirring often, until steaming hot and creamy again.
